subject: Different results in factor loadings in EFA

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Different results in factor loadings in EFA
parts:
I have a problem that I cannot reproduce, but I would like to see where the potential problem is.

This is from the lavaan website, and I keep only the EFA part:

ex5_25 <- read.table("http://statmodel.com/usersguide/chap5/ex5.25.dat")
names(ex5_25) <- paste0("y", 1:12)

model <-
'
efa("efa1")*f1 +
efa("efa1")*f2 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4 + y5 + y6
'

target_m <- matrix(0, 6, 2)
target_m[1:3, 1] <- 1
target_m[4:6, 2] <- 1
target_m

library(lavaan)
fit <- cfa(
  model = model,
  data = ex5_25,
  rotation = "target",
  rotation.args = list(
    orthogonal = TRUE,
    target = target_m
  )
)

This is not exactly the model I ran, but the settings are the same. I found that the results I got from 0.7-3 were different from those in 0.6-19 that I ran earlier this year. Only the factor loadings are different. All other values are the same.

I thought it was due to the version of lavaan. However, when I installed 0.6-19 and ran the analysis again, all the results, including the factor loadings, are identical to those from 0.7-3.

So, it seems that the differences are not due to any difference between 0.6-19 and 0.7-3.

What are the possible reasons for the differences? I guess the differences lie somewhere else, not in lavaan. However, I didn't run sessionInfo() in the script.

I suspect the differences are due to target rotation because only the loadings are different. Does lavaan use another package for the rotation? I can then install an older version of that package to see whether I can reproduce the old results.

-- Shu Fai

messages.author: 8c5a85ec8479672a
messages.subject: Re: Different results in factor loadings in EFA
parts:
Hi Shu Fai, 

I briefly went to look at this and it does seem to be the case that rotation = "target" is not the same across the two versions you mentioned. The loadings' difference was not huge, but it was indeed different. Maybe you didn't really load 0.6-19 after installing it again? 

I just focused on the computation/implementation differences, I don't really have the time to try to understand what exactly is the difference though. Also, lavaan does not use another package for rotation. 

Best,
Felipe.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Different results in factor loadings in EFA
parts:
Since lavaan 0.6-20, rotation = "target" implies rotation = “pst” (only
fixing the zero elements). To get the old "target" results, you need to
use rotation = "target.strict" which takes the values in the target
matrix literally.

Although the results are usually close. This is my output for 0.7-3 for
the ex2.25 example:

Latent Variables:
Estimate Std.Err z-value P(>|z|)
f1 =~ efa1
y1 0.721 0.041 17.665 0.000
y2 0.844 0.041 20.357 0.000
y3 0.716 0.041 17.562 0.000
y4 0.228 0.034 6.653 0.000
y5 0.174 0.031 5.572 0.000
y6 0.205 0.034 6.002 0.000
f2 =~ efa1
y1 0.212 0.034 6.318 0.000
y2 0.207 0.031 6.611 0.000
y3 0.173 0.033 5.228 0.000
y4 0.740 0.042 17.630 0.000
y5 0.796 0.041 19.401 0.000
y6 0.765 0.043 17.948 0.000

And this is 0.6-19:

Latent Variables:
Estimate Std.Err z-value P(>|z|)
f1 =~ efa1
y1 0.721 0.040 17.813 0.000
y2 0.844 0.041 20.460 0.000
y3 0.715 0.040 17.668 0.000
y4 0.227 0.034 6.675 0.000
y5 0.173 0.032 5.464 0.000
y6 0.204 0.034 5.984 0.000
f2 =~ efa1
y1 0.213 0.033 6.379 0.000
y2 0.208 0.032 6.545 0.000
y3 0.174 0.033 5.261 0.000
y4 0.740 0.042 17.807 0.000
y5 0.796 0.041 19.493 0.000
y6 0.765 0.042 18.089 0.000


Similar but not identical. If I use 0.7-3 with rotation =
"target.strict", I do get identical results. I could easily imagine that
for other model/data combinations, the differences are much larger.

But that does not explain why you got the same results with 0.6-19? Best
to restart R/Rstudio after installing another version, to take effect.

Yves.

messages.subject: Re: Different results in factor loadings in EFA
parts:
Dear Felipe and Yves,

Thanks a lot for the information! I checked again on my computer, and the two results are very similar this time, as Yves demonstrated. I thought it was my oversight, or that I had forgotten to restart R, as Yves suggested.

The differences are larger in the real data I am working on, and we used ordered = TRUE in that case. However, when I discretized the data for ex2.25, the results in the two versions were still quite similar, even though the settings are identical to those I used in the real data.

I will try to set "target.strict" and see whether I can reproduce the old results.

Thanks again.

-- Shu Fai
